primary.thesis: As of 2026-07-13 the rules name Dan Jarvis as the sitting Defence Secretary, so the post was filled recently in a reshuffle. UK Defence Secretaries usually serve for years, and a new appointee is rarely moved within six months unless a new Prime Minister takes over or there is a resignation scandal. With only about 5.5 months left in 2026, nobody else is likely to be appointed by 31 Dec 2026, so the market should resolve to 'No next Defence Secretary in 2026'. John Healey was the previous holder, so bringing him back would mean reversing a recent decision. Al Carns is a junior minister, and promoting him straight to the post would need a new leader who wants to reward him.

basket.reason: Jarvis was only recently appointed, and there is little time left in 2026 for a fresh appointment.
Healey was just moved out of the post. Only a completely new PM restoring the old line-up would bring him back.
Going from junior minister straight to Secretary of State in under six months needs a leadership change plus a personal reward, which is unlikely.

failure_narrative: The basket loses if someone other than Jarvis is formally appointed Defence Secretary before year end. The most likely route is a Labour leadership crisis: Starmer is challenged or resigns after poor polling or a revolt, and the new Labour leader forms a new cabinet with a different Defence Secretary. Carns or Healey getting the job would also sink the NO legs. Other routes are Jarvis resigning over a scandal or policy dispute (for example defence spending or procurement), or a second reshuffle to handle a cabinet resignation somewhere else.
hedge_thesis: The primary thesis fails mainly when UK government stability breaks down: a Labour leadership contest or change of PM, with a new cabinet. In those same worlds UK financial markets tend to price political and fiscal risk. A leadership challenge from the left or the soft left raises fears of looser fiscal rules, so gilt yields rise, especially at the long end, and sterling weakens. Contracts on a Labour leadership change, Starmer leaving, or a named successor (Burnham, Streeting, Rayner) winning would pay out in exactly the worlds where a new Defence Secretary is appointed.
